contracts.declared_mechanism: Starlette-style HTTP middleware created by create_middleware(app) and registered on the production app at backend/app_t.py:136; the inner global_handler (decorated with @app.middleware("http"), middleware.py:48-49) short-circuits whitelisted paths (middleware.py:50-52), otherwise calls validate_token_and_refresh(request) (middleware.py:56), which reads the X-Token and X-User-Id headers (middleware.py:20-21), obtains app.state.cache (the Redis client initialized in lifespan at app_t.py:48-55), fetches users:{user_id} and rejects on mismatch with HTTPException(401) (middleware.py:36-39), renews the TTL with state.cache.expire(f"users:{user_id}", Config.EXPIRE_TIME=3600) on success (middleware.py:42), and global_handler converts failures into JSONResponse error responses (middleware.py:57-68) and only reaches call_next after successful validation (middleware.py:71).

contracts.protection_obligation: Every HTTP request reaching the FastAPI application in backend/app_t.py whose path is not in Config.WHITE_LIST must present an X-Token header (Config.TOKEN_HEADER_KEY) together with an X-User-Id header, where X-Token matches the Redis-cached token stored at key users:{X-User-Id} in app.state.cache, as validated by validate_token_and_refresh; the middleware must reject failing requests with 401 (or 500 for unexpected validation errors) via JSONResponse before invoking call_next, so that no endpoint handler executes for unauthenticated requests. (Merged contract: the first-phase and second-phase reviewer obligations describe the same middleware-enforced token gate with a single commit point at call_next.)
scope_limits: Whitelisted paths (Config.WHITE_LIST: /api/login, /api/user/register, /docs, /openapi., /redoc) bypass token validation entirely (middleware.py:50-52; config.py:28).

The guard is generic web authentication applied uniformly to every non-whitelisted HTTP path; the supplied source contains no decorator, registration, callback wiring, tool dispatch, or concrete dataflow binding these guarded operations to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input, so absent such a binding the obligation is ordinary HTTP authentication outside DEC scope.

The gate acts only at the HTTP request boundary: file writes (app_t.py:373-376), database deletes/inserts/updates (app_t.py:399-402, 430-433, 459-462), and agent invocations (app_t.py:215-219, 259) occur downstream of call_next and are not separately gated by per-operation checks in this middleware.

The middleware validates only the X-Token/X-User-Id headers; it does not cross-check user identifiers supplied in endpoint bodies or query parameters (e.g., chat body user_id at app_t.py:191, sessions query user_id at app_t.py:471).
CORS middleware configuration (app_t.py:127-133) is a separate mechanism and outside this contract.
